quizzes.title: Factors Behind the Open War
quizzes.passage:
Pakistan and Afghanistan have disputed several issues along their shared frontier for years, and these disputes lie behind the current confrontation. One issue is cross-border militancy. Pakistan accuses the Afghan Taliban of allegedly sheltering the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan, which is accused of launching attacks across the border into Pakistan.

A second issue concerns the boundary itself. The Durand Line separates the two countries, and its status has been contested for a long time. Afghan governments have historically questioned its legitimacy.

Tensions also turned into direct fighting. Clashes at disputed checkpoints escalated into military confrontation. Pakistan launched an operation against Afghan military bases, and Afghanistan retaliated with airstrikes on Pakistani targets.

The Taliban had returned to full control in 2021 after the US withdrawal, and Pakistan initially welcomed that development. However, tensions resurfaced as cross-border militancy continued. India condemned Pakistan's attacks and reaffirmed its support for Afghanistan's sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence.

questions.q: Afghanistan's objection to the Durand Line is that the agreement was signed under which kind of pressure?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Afghanistan argues the agreement was signed under colonial pressure.

questions.q: Which Pakistani doctrine has been eroded by the Taliban's outreach to India?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Pakistan's strategic depth doctrine has been eroded by the Taliban's outreach to India.

questions.q: Repeated closures of the Torkham crossing pushed Kabul toward which kind of routes?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Torkham closures pushed Kabul toward Iranian routes.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Pakistan considers the Durand Line a legal international boundary.
Reason (R): Afghan forces have resisted Pakistan's border fencing.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but Afghan resistance to fencing does not explain Pakistan's legal view of the boundary.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Durand Line
II. Nur Khan Airbase
III. 12th Division HQ
IV. Strategic depth
List II: A. Erosion by Taliban outreach to India   B. Divided Pashtun tribal populations   C. Airbase in Rawalpindi   D. Division HQ in Quetta
questions.explanation: The Durand Line divided Pashtun populations, Nur Khan is in Rawalpindi, 12th Division HQ is in Quetta, and strategic depth has been eroded by the Taliban's outreach to India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Afghanistan officially recognises the Durand Line as a permanent border.
II. Repeated closures of the Torkham crossing have hurt Afghan trade.
III. Pakistan was one of the few countries to recognise the Taliban regime in the 1990s.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is false because Afghanistan does not officially recognise the Durand Line, while II and III are stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Taliban captured Kabul in 1996.
II. Afghanistan's monarchy ended in 1979.
III. The Shahtoot Dam Project of 2021 was launched to provide drinking water to Kabul.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the monarchy ended in 1973, not 1979.

quizzes.title: Border Strains and Military Escalation
quizzes.passage:
Pakistan and Afghanistan have been in dispute for a long time, and the current fighting followed a series of incidents. Pakistan launched an operation against Afghan military bases. In response, Afghanistan carried out airstrikes on Pakistani targets, which showed that the conflict had moved beyond the border.

Several issues lie behind the confrontation. The Afghan Taliban is accused of sheltering a militant group that attacks Pakistan, and the two sides also disagree over the border between them. Pakistan regards the Durand Line as a permanent international boundary, while Afghan governments have historically disputed its legitimacy.

Trade has been another source of strain. Crossings on the border have been shut more than once, and these closures have damaged Afghan trade. The disruption pushed the Afghan government to look for other routes, and it added to the mistrust between the two countries.

Pakistan's own policy has also been affected. For a long time it relied on a doctrine that treated Afghanistan as a source of leverage. The Taliban's outreach to India has weakened that approach.

questions.q: Which Pakistani airbase in Rawalpindi was targeted by Afghan airstrikes?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Nur Khan Airbase in Rawalpindi as one of the targets of Afghanistan's airstrikes.

questions.q: Afghan airstrikes also hit the 12th Division HQ; in which Pakistani city is that headquarters located?
questions.explanation: The booklet places the 12th Division HQ in Quetta.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation TTP stand for?
questions.explanation: The booklet expands TTP as Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan.

questions.q: What is the length of the Durand Line, in km?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the Durand Line's length as 2640 km.

questions.q: Which doctrine, which treated Afghanistan as a source of leverage, has been eroded by the Taliban's outreach to India?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the erosion of Pakistan's strategic depth doctrine by the Taliban's outreach to India.

questions.q: In which year did Pakistan inherit the Durand Line as a border after independence?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Pakistan inherited the border after independence in 1947.

questions.q: Repeated closures of the Torkham crossing pushed which Afghan capital toward Iranian trade routes?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the closures pushed Kabul toward Iranian routes.

quizzes.title: What the Conflict Means for India
quizzes.passage:
Fighting between Pakistan and Afghanistan has consequences that reach beyond the two countries. The booklet discusses the effects on India under a separate heading, covering India's western border, its security and its trade links.

Afghanistan has seen many changes of government. Its monarchy ended in 1973, and a communist government backed by the Soviet Union followed. After the US withdrawal in August 2021, the Taliban regained full control of the country.

Pakistan first welcomed the Taliban's return, but tensions resurfaced as cross-border militancy continued. The Afghan Taliban is allegedly sheltering the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan, which is accused of cross-border attacks. Border crossings have also been shut more than once, and these closures have hurt Afghan trade.

The fighting began when Pakistan launched an operation against Afghan military bases. Afghanistan replied with airstrikes on Pakistani targets, and the confrontation became a direct military one.

questions.q: Afghanistan is described as a crossroad between South Asia and Central Asia, and between South Asia and which other region?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Afghanistan as a crossroad between South Asia and the Middle East as well as Central Asia.

questions.q: What did India do regarding Pakistan's attacks on Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India condemned Pakistan's attacks.

questions.q: Along with sovereignty and territorial integrity, what did India reaffirm for Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: India reaffirmed Afghanistan's independence alongside its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A full-scale conflict risks an Afghan refugee inflow onto India's borders.
Reason (R): Prolonged instability risks allowing ISIS-K to regroup and expand across South Asia.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the risk of ISIS-K regrouping does not explain the risk of a refugee inflow.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Connectivity Risks
II. Terror Spillover
III. Refugee Pressure
IV. LoC Relief
List II: A. Reduced infiltration pressure along the LoC   B. Afghan refugee inflow onto India's borders   C. Access to INSTC jeopardised   D. ISIS-K regroup and expand across South Asia
questions.explanation: Connectivity risks affect INSTC access, terror spillover means ISIS-K expansion, refugee pressure means an Afghan refugee inflow, and LoC relief means reduced infiltration pressure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Afghanistan officially recognises the Durand Line as a permanent border.
II. The conflict jeopardises India's access to the INSTC.
III. Afghanistan argues that the Durand Line was a temporary arrangement.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is false because Afghanistan does not officially recognise the Durand Line, while II and III are stated in the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Taliban captured Kabul in 1996.
II. Afghanistan's monarchy ended in 1979.
III. The Shahtoot Dam Project of 2021 was launched to provide drinking water to Kabul.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the monarchy ended in 1973, not 1979.

quizzes.title: Implications of the Conflict for India
quizzes.passage:
The war between Pakistan and Afghanistan carries implications for India, which the booklet groups under a heading of its own. The effects are described for several areas, including India's western border, its security environment and its trade links.

Afghanistan has been through many changes of government. Its monarchy ended in 1973, and a communist government backed by the Soviet Union followed. After the US withdrawal in August 2021, the Taliban regained full control of the country.

Pakistan first welcomed that development, expecting strategic alignment. However, tensions resurfaced as cross-border militancy continued. Border crossings have also been shut more than once, and these closures have hurt Afghan trade.

The military phase began when Pakistan launched an operation against Afghan military bases. Afghanistan replied with airstrikes on Pakistani targets, and the confrontation became a direct military one. The booklet presents these events as the background to its discussion of what the conflict means for India.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation INSTC stand for?
questions.explanation: The booklet expands INSTC as the International North-South Transport Corridor.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation ISIS-K stand for?
questions.explanation: The booklet expands ISIS-K as the Islamic State Khorasan Province.

questions.q: A full-scale conflict risks an inflow of which people onto India's borders?
questions.explanation: The booklet warns that a full-scale conflict risks an Afghan refugee inflow onto India's borders.

questions.q: Escalation on the western border may reduce Pakistan's infiltration pressure along which line?
questions.explanation: The booklet says escalation may compel Pakistan to reduce infiltration pressure along the Line of Control.

questions.q: What did India do to Pakistan's attacks on Afghanistan? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India condemned Pakistan's attacks on Afghanistan.

questions.q: India reaffirmed Afghanistan's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and also which other principle?
questions.explanation: India reaffirmed Afghanistan's independence along with its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

questions.q: Afghanistan is described as a crossroad between South Asia and Central Asia, and between South Asia and which other region?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Afghanistan as a crossroad between South Asia and the Middle East as well as Central Asia.
